front: How is a column heading written in a results table?
back: Quantity / unit, e.g. $l\,/\,\text{m}$ or $T^2\,/\,\text{s}^2$; units do not appear in the body of the table.

front: To what precision are raw readings recorded?
back: To the resolution of the instrument, with every reading in a column to the same number of decimal places (e.g. 0.460 m, not 0.46 m, from a millimetre rule).

front: How many significant figures should a calculated value have?
back: The same as the least precise raw data used, or one more.

front: How many readings and what range for a straight-line graph?
back: At least six sets, spread evenly over as wide a range as the apparatus allows, each repeated (all values recorded).
$\dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ from two points on the line more than half its length apart; unit = unit of $y$ / unit of $x$.

front: How do you find the intercept when the x-axis has a false origin?
back: Calculate it: $c = y - mx$, using the gradient and one point on the line.
Use simple steps (1, 2 or 5 per large square) and make the points cover at least half the grid in each direction.
One thin line (or smooth curve) with the points balanced on either side along its length; not forced through the origin or any point.

front: Why time 20 oscillations rather than one?
back: The reaction-time uncertainty (about 0.2–0.3 s) is shared over 20 cycles, so the percentage uncertainty in the period is much smaller.
$T^2$ against $l$: a straight line through the origin with gradient $4\pi^2/g$.
